summary: Previous observation of a UFO: no details.
description: Brief account dated January 27, 2009, of an observation made in the evening in the early 1990s in Côte-d'Or. No details are provided regarding the date (the day and month are given arbitrarily) or the phenomenon observed. No further information was obtained despite our request.

summary: Brief observation of the slow and silent passage of a phenomenon delimited by three white lights in the summer night sky: lack of information.
description: In 2008, a witness reported an observation made during a summer between 1990 and 1993 (the date of June 1, 1990, is given arbitrarily). One evening, around 11 p.m., as he was preparing to go camping with a friend in his garden, the witness, about ten years old, observed from the entrance of his tent the arrival in the clear sky of three white lights outlining a large, opaque triangular shape. The phenomenon moved silently and very slowly over the village on a straight trajectory. During the brief observation, the witness had the impression that the main triangle was formed by a series of smaller triangles connected to other lights. The young boy was frightened, and his friend did not have time to see the phenomenon. Only one witness statement was recorded. This statement was not usable by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomy). Indeed, this is an observation made by a child and reported 18 years after the events, without specifying the date (or even the year) of the observation. GEIPAN is not even able to search its database and compare it with similar testimonies in the same location and/or date range. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Presence of a circular mark on the ground of crushed grass; differentiated growth of the affected grass compared to the rest of the garden: lack of information.
description: 2008 testimony recounts an observation made between 1988 and 1990 (the witness no longer remembers the exact date (spring/summer 1988-1990). The date of April 1, 1988, is given arbitrarily). During the spring or summer of 1988-1990, three people arriving at their property were intrigued by a mark on the ground at the edge of a hedge. This circular mark, approximately 20 centimeters wide, resulted from the crushing of grass. The resulting circle had an outer diameter of about 2 meters. This mark remained visible for several months, evidenced by the uneven growth of the affected grass compared to the rest of the garden. Only one testimony was collected. This testimony was deemed unusable by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). Indeed, it did not describe a UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) but a circle. on the ground with no possibility of linking it to a UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) because no UAP has been described. GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.
